name: Plug-door hinge
summary: A door that plugs its opening from inside is pulled in, tipped out and swung flat outside by a goose-neck hinge steered by an S-shaped track.

ratio.typical: door turns 180° for 157° of hinge tube; about 10° of it while the tube is held

topology.notes: ground (wall, hinge post, track), crank, goose-neck, guide arm and door; the higher pair is the follower in its track: 3 x 4 - 2 x 5 - 1 = 1; count includes ground

explain.motion: The hand on the door moves the whole linkage, and the follower on the guide arm runs along the fixed S-shaped track. The first arc of the track is centred on the crank's pin to the guide arm, so for the first 26 mm of travel the hinge tube stands still: the door moves as the coupler of a four-bar, pulls in out of its seat and turns about 10°. The track then bends the other way, the hinge tube turns 157° and the goose-neck carries the door out through the opening and round until it lies flat outside the wall, turned 180°. Closing runs the same path back.
explain.forces: The track takes the linkage's spare freedom, so the groove sets the door's whole path and the hand only supplies the effort along it. The roller bears on one wall of the groove or the other, hardest where the track bends tightly. Closed, the stop lips sit on the inside of the jambs, so a push on the door from inside presses it into its seat instead of out.
explain.benefits: The door needs no hinge cut in the wall or in its own face, and it ends folded flat against the outside, clear of the opening. One hand moves it through the whole compound motion.
explain.limits: The track and the long bent guide arm take room inside beside the opening, and the tight bend of the track needs a hard roller and liners. The geometry is sensitive: a small change to a link or to the track brings a dead point or a clash.

build.ground: the wall with its opening, the fixed post the hinge tube turns on, and the plate with the S-shaped groove
build.defining_relations: Mobility 3 x 4 - 2 x 5 - 1 = 1. The follower F at travel s on the track and the hinge tube H fix the crank's pin G as a dyad (HG = 40.6, GF = 76.6); the crank then places K, and the door's pins N and D close as a dyad on K (goose-neck KN = 74.5) and D (ND = 21.1 on the door). The first track arc has radius GF and is centred on G in the closed pose, so while F runs on it the crank holds still and the door moves as the coupler of the four-bar K-N-D-G.
build.notes: Range: follower travel 0 to 167.45 mm and back each cycle (the open stop 0.05 mm short of the end of the 167.5 mm track, so the door stops just short of 180°), hinge tube 0° to -157.4°, door 0° to -180° (clockwise in plan). Plan frame: x along the wall, y > 0 inside, wall from y = 0 to 10, opening from x = 0 to 100. The patent's numbers: H is the hinge tube 16, K 26, N 32, D 40, G 66, F the follower 48 in the track 44. Both dyads keep their side over the motion: least transmission angle 41° at G (H-G-F) and 45° at N (K-N-D), so no dead point. The track: arc 1 R 76.6 about G for 26.2 mm (the dwell), arc 2 R 12.9 the same way for 30.8 mm, arc 3 R 70.6 the other way for 110.5 mm, tangent at the joins. The goose-neck and the guide arm's arm to D are hooked: straight bars would strike the jamb and the door's edge.

review.note: T2 review of the record, 2026-11-15 (#288), on the chosen design of #286 unchanged: keep. Six phases from the solved motion (travel, hinge tube, door): 1 closed, lips on the jambs (0 mm, 0°, 0°); 2 pulled in out of the seat (9.9 mm, 0°, -4.6°); 3 end of the dwell arc (26.2 mm, 0°, -10.1°); 4 free edge out through the opening (47.8 mm, -19.2°, -37.4°); 5 swinging round (85.6 mm, -68.2°, -90°); 6 open, flat outside (167.45 mm, -157.4°, -180°). Solve checks: the hinge tube holds still (within 1e-9°) over the first 26.2 mm, while the door turns 10.1° as the coupler of the four-bar K-N-D-G, because the first arc of the track is centred on G; then the tube turns 157.4° and the door 180°; least transmission angle 41.5° at G and 44.7° at N, so neither dyad nears a dead point; poses at cycles 2 and 3 equal cycle 1. The text was read against the motion; its numbers are the claims. Decisions: hand operated (V5 manual) with the follower run along the track closed to open and back (target-path track, oscillate), the hand driver on the hinge tube read back off the pose; the open stop 0.05 mm short of the track end so the door stops just short of 180° (the turn output would wrap at 180°); traces the free-edge corner (comet, equal-time ticks), the hinge-edge corner and the follower; plot door angle against hinge-tube angle, where the dwell reads as the vertical run at 0°; PLAN view (opens tilted); no overlays and no focus yet, both judged again on the finished build. Teaching strings name the mechanism only: a wall with an opening and a door with stop lips, no aircraft parts. Judged on the finished build (2026-11-16): the follower roller in its groove is the part to watch (focus) and gets a section view across the track; no overlays, the traces and the plot carry the lesson.

claims.text: for the first 26 mm of travel the hinge tube stands still
pulls in out of its seat and turns about 10°
lies flat outside the wall, turned 180°
follower travel 0 to 167.45 mm and back each cycle

views.note: the roller on the guide arm, held both ways in the groove: the track takes the linkage's spare freedom

examples.detail: A plug door seated from inside is drawn in, turned edgewise and swung flat against the outside of the fuselage on goose-neck hinge arms.

examples.use: Doors that must seal from the inside
examples.detail: A door whose stops bear on the inside of its frame needs a hinge that first draws it inward before it can swing out.
